subject: Acme pricing & context-length profiling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can model pricing and a pilot plan: 

1) Workload profile (what I captured on the call):
   - Primary use case: enhanced search + summarization for customer support knowledge base.
   - Typical user request = 1 prompt + model completion (search + synthesized response).

2) Data we need to finalize costs: could you confirm the following rough numbers? a short reply with the bullets is perfect.
   - avg prompt tokens per request (prompt + context)
   - avg completion tokens per request
   - expected queries/day (or per month) and any weekly/peak patterns
   - % of requests that require extended context (need 8k / 32k / 128k)
   - retention / logging needs (token-level logs or only aggregated billing)

3) Budget/target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to keep unit cost to a target $/1M tokens — can you share a target $/1M tokens or a monthly budget range we should aim for?

Attached is a quick token-estimate template I ran through from our call (acme_token_estimates.xlsx) and our standard pricing summary (redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf). Once you send the numbers above I’ll run scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and propose a target price per 1M tokens aligned to total spend and performance SLOs.

Next steps: if it helps I can put together three scenarios by EOD tomorrow: pilot (hosted), reserved monthly commit (Dedicated small), and Dedicated + 32k context option. Also happy to set a follow-up next week to walk through.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

---
Attachments: acme_token_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood_pricing_sheet.pdf (pricing summary)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Bethany Li <bethany.li@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary. See answers inline below. I ran the numbers with our engineering lead and attached a short internal note.

- avg prompt tokens per request: ~450 (we include a 2–3 paragraph user prompt + 3–4 context chunks from the KB)
- avg completion tokens per request: ~220 (most replies are concise summaries)
- expected queries: ~160k requests / month (roughly 5.0M tokens/month total today; expecting growth to ~15–20M tokens/mo in 6–9 months)
- peak vs baseline: ~3x daily peak during support surge windows (11am–2pm PT)
- % needing extended context: ~18% require >8k context; ~6% require >=32k; <1% for 128k
- retention/logging: need request/response dumps for sampling and quality monitoring for 90 days; aggregated billing is fine for finance
- target unit economics: we’re targeting $150–$300 / 1M tokens depending on latency and SLAs; overall monthly budget range target $20k–$40k initially (may expand if we see value)

We attached our internal token-estimates.pdf (internal) — please let me know if you want raw logs sample or a small export we can share.

Alex
Alex Turner, Head of AI Platform
Acme Corp
alex.turner@acmecorp.com

---
Attachments: acme_internal_notes.pdf (internal token breakout)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Alex — great, this is exactly what we needed, thanks. A few comments based on your numbers: 

1) Unit economics framing: with your current ~5M tokens/month, and expected growth to 15–20M, the best fit normally looks like this:
   - Pilot/hosted (no commit): cost may land around $200–$350 / 1M tokens depending on model selection and context requirements (higher for heavy 32k usage).
   - Dedicated reserved (monthly commit): we can typically hit $120–$200 / 1M tokens at the 15–20M token range depending on batching and KV cache hit rates.
   - Dedicated + 32k opt-in for the 6% heavy context requests: add a small premium (~15–25%) for the portion of traffic that requires the wider context due to memory & serving overheads.

2) Suggested next step: I’ll run three concrete scenarios in the spreadsheet you already have — hosted pilot, 12-month reserved commit targetting 15M/mo, and a hybrid where 6% of traffic is routed to 32k nodes. I’ll include modeled $/1M tokens for each scenario and an expected monthly spend. I’ll also flag where Dedicated makes sense from a latency/SLA perspective.

3) Security/logs: Priyom, can you confirm retention options for request/response dumps (90 days) and what we can provide for SOC/audit evidence for the pilot? If there are any constraints that would materially affect cost, flag them.

Can we tentatively schedule a 30-min pricing review on Thursday 31 Mar at 11:00am PT? If that works I’ll send an invite.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme pricing & context-length profiling

Thanks Marissa — Thursday 11:00am PT works for me.

Alex, quick note from infra side: if we proceed with a hybrid (hosted + 32k pool) we’ll want a small carve-out in the SLA for the 32k nodes (cold-starts and scheduling). Priyom — I’ll sync with you offline on the logs retention implementation and SOC artifacts we need to hand to Acme for the pilot.

-Jordan
